note: Interim reading 2026-10-04 (day 9 of 14; the dated V5 record stays for 2026-10-09). `next_census.py --since 7 --repo /opt/fabrik` printed a bare `V5: PASS` before 95155b6f5; re-run after it, it prints `V5: PASS — 0 open next item(s) <= 0 qualifying session(s), 3 live claim(s)` — a vacuous pass. Classes line at that run: 12797 NEXT lines over 1648 transcript files (names-item 1269, none 220, operator-decision 715, blocked 8, free-text 10585). A probe run minutes later over 1651 files found 34 ending on a NEXT line (18 names-item, 7 none, 5 free-text, 4 operator-decision) and 1617 carrying none. The five session-final free-text values, none matching _is_anchor: a live fabrik-lib session's 'when <seats> report, adjudicate them and send …' step (its wording moved with each of its turns across three runs), 'awaiting your reply — once the key is in .env, I run …' (trade-intelligence, main and a worktree), 'merge the next merge request from agent-2 or agent-3 …' (tryton-crm), 'awaiting your reply' (youtube) — each a transient step or a wait, none a thread worth persisting. So on this small sample (n=5) _is_anchor drops nothing worth keeping, and about half of the sessions that end on a NEXT name an item id. Caveat for the dated reading: the census counts NEXT lines more strictly than the harvest, counts every transcript file as a session and never counts the hub's worktree sessions — W-a9de5fb3 fixes that first.
